analysis.title: A.O. Smith Corp. (AOS): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: AOS reported 3Q26 adj EPS of $0.93 vs GS estimate and FactSet consensus of $0.90. The beat came mainly from EBIT margin of 18.6%, 83bps above the GS model (+$0.04).
Other EPS bridge items vs GS model: lower tax rate +$0.02, interest expense +$0.01, revenue down 0.2% vs GS +3.8% forecast ($0.04), other income ($0.01).
Results reflect navigation of weak residential demand and rising inflation, helped by cost actions and productivity. North America boiler sales were strong and Leonard Valve contributed.

On Oct. 27 AOS announced a definitive agreement to divest an 81% interest in its China business to CPE. The deal values operations at ~$400mn on a cash-free, debt-free basis, excluding a long-term brand licensing royalty stream that management estimates at $500+mn NPV. AOS expects to repatriate ~$80mn in cash. The deal concludes the strategic review announced in July 2025.
Adjusting for the divestiture, 2026 sales are now expected up 4% at the midpoint with adj. EPS of $3.47, per the press release.
North America revenue rose 3% (+1% excl. Leonard Valve) vs GS +2%, with boiler volumes, carryover pricing and a $15mn Leonard Valve gain partly offset by weak residential water heater volumes.

North America adj. EBIT margin fell 57bps YOY to 23.6%, 12bps above GS. Lost operating leverage and higher steel and freight costs were more than offset by pricing, IEEPA tariff refunds, boilers and Leonard Valve.
Rest of World revenue fell 7% YOY vs GS +5% estimate, including $5mn favorable FX. China sales fell 17% ex-FX on macro and the strategic review. Adj. EBIT margin fell 196bps YOY to 5.4% vs GS 6.5%.

Net debt/EBITDA was 0.6x, similar to 2Q26 and above 0.0x a year ago, with $235mn in cash and short-term securities. AOS repurchased 4.2mn shares for $260.6mn in the first nine months vs a ~$300mn full-year target, with ~1.6mn shares left on the authorization. The dividend was raised 6% on Oct. 12 to $0.38.
GS rates AOS Sell with a $55 12-month price target (9.5x Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA), implying 9.6% downside from $60.86.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q beat was driven by margin, while revenue missed GS estimates and residential demand and China remain weak. Price $60.86 implies 9.6% downside.

sector_views.rationale: Residential water heater demand is weak amid a housing deceleration, though commercial and boiler demand is holding up.

earnings_insights: AOS 3Q26 adj EPS $0.93 reported (adjusted) vs GS estimate and FactSet consensus $0.90, reported 10/29/2026.
3Q26 adj EBIT margin 18.6% reported, 83bps above the GS model.
3Q26 revenue down 0.2% YOY reported vs GS forecast of +3.8%.
North America 3Q26 revenue +3% reported vs GS +2%. Segment adj. EBIT margin 23.6% reported, down 57bps YOY and 12bps above GS.
Rest of World 3Q26 revenue -7% YOY reported vs GS +5% estimate. Segment adj. EBIT margin 5.4% reported vs GS 6.5% estimate.
Company guidance after adjusting for the China divestiture: 2026 sales up 4% at the midpoint, adj. EPS $3.47.
GS estimates: 2026E EPS $3.75, 2027E $4.00, 2028E $4.40. Quarterly GS estimates: 9/26E $0.90, 12/26E $0.97, 3/27E $0.90 (these predate the 3Q print).
risk_factors: Weak residential water heater demand and a decelerating housing market.
Rising inflation in input costs, especially steel, resins and freight.
China weakness, with sales down 17% ex-FX, and execution risk on the 81% divestiture to CPE.
Upside risks to the Sell view per GS: successful new products, lower raw material costs, continued commercial share gains, effective capital allocation.
